success_criteria: Installation completes on Node 18 and Node 20 with no direct legacy hapi/inert/Babel 6/node-sass/request/moment/bootstrap-vue packages.
Webpack 5 development build produces usable JS/CSS assets with Babel 7, Dart Sass, Vue 2.7, and no removed webpack-dev-server schema options.
ESLint 8 runs across ui and js and exits 0 without suppressing the entire upgraded surface.
The bounded production startup reaches the renderable root page at http://localhost:8080/ and shuts down cleanly.
The focused Mocha Node-upgrade suite initializes Hapi 21 with Inert 7 and verifies asynchronous GET/POST adapter response and error semantics; all three tests pass with no failed assertion markers.
All seven requested direct Node integration/template scripts exit 0 with no failed assertion markers.
Search/navigation, ID resolution/404s, detail descriptions, ontology viewer, phenotype analysis, Phenogrid, API/JSON endpoints, and Bootstrap interactions pass with no browser console errors.
Live GOlr/Solr, SciGraph, OwlSim, and Biolink contracts are either verified against checked-in configuration or explicitly reported as environmental blockers; an app root 200 alone is not sufficient.
Only planned files plus at most the bounded dependency-call-site expansion allowance change; pre-existing unrelated worktree edits and generated artifacts are preserved.

rollback_strategy: Revert the single final execution commit created by the executor.
planning_notes: The ImpactReport was authoritative, but GitNexus had an empty index, so planning retained its reduced-confidence filesystem evidence. Whole-file reads were required for package.json, the small Babel/ESLint configs, Makefile, webapp_launcher.js, the relevant feature files, and tests/test-common.js because isolated ranges could not establish scripts, ports, harness completion, or exact browser routes; other source inspection stayed around reported ranges. The user explicitly requires Vue 2.7 as an interim step: retain vue-router 3 and the Vue 2 constructor/plugin model; do not introduce Vue 3, vue-router 4, bootstrap-vue-next, or a full rewrite. Existing dirty-worktree changes, untracked node_modules/dist/package-lock/webpack-assets, and user test edits predate execution and must be inventoried and preserved; patch only intended hunks and never clean/reset the worktree. All commands were inferred at the repository root. package.json defines wbs-build, wbs-lint, and start; webapp_launcher.js and webapp.js establish port 8080 and a renderable root page, so http://localhost:8080/ is the startup health/browser URL. npm install is intentionally used instead of npm ci because package-lock.json is an untracked/generated upgrade artifact that must be reconciled to the new manifest. GNU make is unavailable in this workspace, so the seven explicit npm-exec/cross-env Node commands are the documented equivalent of the requested make test suite. The ImpactReport did not include three harness files named explicitly by the user; tests/disease-phenotype-test.js, tests/golr-owlsim-test.js, and tests/full-tmpl.js.tests are therefore labeled scope expansions needed to make that approved suite meaningful on Node 18. External service versions remain unknown and require the declared live checks; failures due solely to unavailable historical services must be reported, not hidden. generated_test_commands/files remain empty for the test-generation stage. A scope expansion limit of 6 is pre-authorized because simultaneous Hapi 16-to-21, webpack/dev-server, Bootstrap 4-to-5, and Axios major transitions have unusually broad direct-call surfaces; it applies only to previously unplanned files whose bounded check fails from a direct call to a dependency already listed here, never to unrelated refactors or new dependency upgrades.
plan_summary: Implement 52 line-aware file changes covering the Node 18/20 dependency/toolchain upgrade, retain Vue 2.7, migrate Hapi/webpack/Bootstrap runtime boundaries, and validate through install/build/lint/bounded startup, focused Mocha coverage, seven direct Node tests, browser flows, and external-service contract checks.
